The book begins by saying what it is: the ancient word of the K'iche' people, written down again "now, under the word of God", because the original book, the Popol Vuh, can no longer be seen. It names the creators in a long litany — the Builder and Shaper, the Bearer and Begetter, Tepeu and Q'ucumatz, the old pair Xpiyacoc and Xmucane — and tells how the world was measured out like a maize field, four corners and four sides. Then the account itself: before anything existed there was only the still sea and the empty sky, silent in the dark. Tepeu and Q'ucumatz lay glittering in the water under quetzal feathers. The Heart of Sky, Huracan, came to them; they talked, worried and agreed, and planned the dawn and the beings who would one day honour them. They said "Earth!" and the earth rose, the mountains came up out of the water like a mist, the forests covered them, and the waters were divided among the hills.
